<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a category and let
<MATH_0002> be a representable functor.
Choose an object <MATH_0003> of <MATH_0004> and an isomorphism <MATH_0005>.
The Yoneda lemma guarantees that the pair <MATH_0006>
is unique up to unique isomorphism. The object
<MATH_0007> is called an object <TEXTITOPEN_0001>representing<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> <MATH_0008>.
By the Yoneda lemma the transformation <MATH_0009> corresponds to a unique
element <MATH_0010>. This element is called the <TEXTITOPEN_0002>universal object<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>.
It has the property that for <MATH_0011> the map
<MATH_0012>
is a bijection. Thus <MATH_0013> is universal in the sense that every element
of <MATH_0014> is equal to the image of <MATH_0015> via <MATH_0016> for a unique morphism
<MATH_0017> in <MATH_0018>.
